props.title: Night of the Demon
props.initialSlug: Skeptic faces ancient curse in supernatural clash

sections.content: Night of the Demon (1957) stands as a masterpiece of psychological horror, directed by Jacques Tourneur who previously crafted the influential Cat People (1942). The film adapts M.R. James's story "Casting the Runes," following skeptical professor John Holden investigating a satanic cult. Tourneur's masterful direction creates mounting dread through suggestion and shadow, similar to his work in I Walked with a Zombie (1943). The film's influence echoes through later supernatural thrillers like The Devil Rides Out (1968) and inspired Kate Bush's song "Hounds of Love."

sections.content: The film's controversial demon effects, added by producer Hal E. Chester against Tourneur's wishes, actually enhance the supernatural elements while maintaining psychological ambiguity. This tension between visible horror and suggested terror influenced later British horror films like The Innocents (1961) and The Devil's Own (1966). Dana Andrews delivers a compelling performance as the rationalist forced to confront the supernatural, establishing a character type later seen in films like The Legend of Hell House (1973).

Tourneur's use of light and shadow creates a masterclass in atmospheric horror, drawing from his noir background in films like Out of the Past (1947). The film's exploration of rationalism versus supernatural belief predates similar themes in The Exorcist (1973) and Angel Heart (1987), while its rural English setting and occult elements influenced folk horror classics like The Wicker Man (1973). sections.content: The film's blend of modern skepticism with ancient evil established a template followed by countless supernatural thrillers. Its influence can be seen in everything from Blood on Satan's Claw (1971) to Drag Me to Hell (2009). The character of Julian Karswell, played brilliantly by Niall MacGinnis, created the archetype of the erudite occultist, influencing characters in films like The Devil Rides Out (1968) and Doctor Strange (2016).
